medicare_compliance_rule: Medicare (CMS) requires documented usage of the PAP device for at least 4 hours per night on at least 70% of nights during any single consecutive 30-day period within the first 90 days of therapy. If this is not met and re-evaluated, coverage for the device can be discontinued and therapy must be re-qualified from the start.
escalation_policy: If the patient or record shows a clinical red flag (central/mixed apnea, cardiac arrhythmia, treatment-emergent central apnea, conflicting or missing chart data, or a vulnerable/non-verbal patient who cannot self-report), the agent stops short of taking an automated action (auto-sending an order request, auto-calling the patient) and instead logs the case for a human Respiratory Therapist / clinician to review and decide next steps.

barrier_tips.mask_leak: High leak is usually a fit issue, not a machine issue. Try tightening just the straps that are gapping, and if it keeps leaking after refitting, ask about a different mask style (nasal pillows vs. full-face) at your next supply order.
barrier_tips.forgetting: Keep the mask on the nightstand, not in a drawer, and pair putting it on with something you already do every night, like brushing your teeth or setting an alarm.
barrier_tips.discomfort: Comfort settings can help a lot: turning on ramp (so pressure starts low and builds up) and using the heated humidifier if you're getting a dry nose or throat.
barrier_tips.noise: Some noise is normal, but a sudden change often means the filter needs replacing or the mask has a leak. Worth checking both before assuming the machine itself is the problem.
barrier_tips.claustrophobia: Starting with the mask on for short periods while awake (watching TV, reading) can help you get used to the sensation before relying on it to fall asleep.
barrier_tips.travel_disruption: Bringing the machine on trips, even short ones, and keeping the routine the same helps avoid the multi-day gaps that hurt the compliance percentage the most.

barrier_patient_lines.mask_leak: Honestly the mask keeps leaking air and it wakes me up, so some nights I just give up on it.
barrier_patient_lines.discomfort: It's just uncomfortable, I don't sleep well with it on so I take it off partway through the night.
barrier_patient_lines.noise: It's been louder than I remember, it's hard to fall asleep with the noise.
barrier_patient_lines.forgetting: I've just been forgetting some nights, or I fall asleep before I put it on.
barrier_patient_lines.travel_disruption: I've had a few nights away and didn't bring it, and it's been hard to get back into the routine.

barrier_followup_lines.mask_leak: Last time we spoke you mentioned the mask was leaking -- has refitting it helped at all?
barrier_followup_lines.discomfort: When we talked before, you'd mentioned the mask felt uncomfortable -- has that gotten any better?
barrier_followup_lines.noise: You'd mentioned the machine seemed louder than expected last time -- is that still going on?
barrier_followup_lines.forgetting: Last time you mentioned some nights you just forgot to put it on -- how's that been since?
barrier_followup_lines.travel_disruption: You'd mentioned travel had thrown off your routine last time -- how's it been since you got back into it?

dme_needs.central_apnea_component_at_diagnosis: Central/mixed apnea component present -- not a routine CPAP-pressure fix.
dme_needs.treatment_emergent_central_apnea: Treatment-emergent central sleep apnea documented -- complex, physician-managed.
dme_needs.cardiac_arrhythmia_history: Cardiac arrhythmia in history -- coordinate with cardiology/physician before equipment changes.
dme_needs.residual_ahi_uncontrolled: Residual AHI still elevated on current max settings -- may need physician-directed titration, not a standard supply order.
dme_needs.non_verbal_patient_caregiver_required: Patient is non-verbal / relies on a caregiver to report symptoms -- route through caregiver and clinician, not an automated request.
dme_needs.pressure_setting_conflict_vs_titration: Chart shows conflicting pressure settings between the titration study and the device -- data integrity issue, needs a clinician/tech to confirm the correct setting before any order goes out.

compliance.non_verbal_patient_caregiver_required: Patient is non-verbal / relies on a caregiver -- route outreach through the caregiver and a clinician, not an automated call.
compliance.central_apnea_component_at_diagnosis: Central/mixed apnea component present -- low adherence here may be clinical, not behavioral; a clinician should assess before more outreach calls.
compliance.treatment_emergent_central_apnea: Treatment-emergent central sleep apnea documented -- complex case, physician-managed.
compliance.cardiac_arrhythmia_history: Cardiac arrhythmia in history -- coordinate with the care team before continued outreach.
